title: Best AI Tools for Insurance Brokers (2026 Guide)
summary: Compare CopyCat, Fathom, Circleback, Sonant, Canopy Connect, Broker Buddha, and Quandri across seven insurance brokerage workflows.
body_markdown:
The best tools by broker workflow


- [CopyCat](https://www.runcopycat.com/) is our recommendation for insurance sales: it turns commercial and personal lines quote documents into branded, editable proposals and side-by-side comparisons.
- [Fathom](https://www.fathom.ai/) and[Circleback](https://circleback.ai/) are the meeting-note picks. Fathom is the straightforward capture-and-summary choice; Circleback stands out for customizable post-meeting automations.
- [Sonant](https://www.sonant.ai/) is the phone AI pick because it is built around insurance call routing, quote intake, routine servicing, scheduling, and agency-system updates.
- [Canopy Connect](https://www.usecanopy.com/insurance-data-intake) fits policy-data intake,[Broker Buddha](https://www.brokerbuddha.com/) fits applications and submissions, and[Quandri](https://www.quandri.io/) fits personal lines renewal automation.
- Start with one bottleneck, test the tool on real agency work, and require human review anywhere the output can affect coverage, advice, or a client record.


The best AI tool for an insurance broker is not the product with the longest feature list. It is the product that removes a specific piece of work without separating the producer from the client. For most agencies, the clearest opportunities sit around sales deliverables, meetings, phone calls, data intake, submissions, and renewals.


This guide names a focused pick for each job. We make CopyCat, so our recommendation in the sales category is not independent. The other selections are based on the vendors' published product materials, their fit with an agency workflow, and whether the output can move cleanly into the systems a brokerage already uses.


## What are the best AI tools for insurance brokers?


Broker workflow Best AI tool Why it fits


Sales proposals and quote comparison[CopyCat](https://www.runcopycat.com/) Creates agency-branded commercial and personal lines proposals from carrier documents, with editable output and source citations.


Meeting notes and sales-call follow-up[Fathom](https://www.fathom.ai/) Captures transcripts, summaries, action items, and searchable meeting context, with CRM connections for sales teams.


Meeting notes with custom automations[Circleback](https://circleback.ai/) Turns meeting transcripts into structured insights and can trigger CRM, Slack, Notion, Zapier, and other post-meeting actions.


Inbound calls and phone service[Sonant](https://www.sonant.ai/) Insurance-specific voice AI for call answering, routing, quote intake, routine servicing, scheduling, and post-call notes.


Policy-data and declaration-page intake[Canopy Connect](https://www.usecanopy.com/insurance-data-intake) Collects permissioned carrier data or extracts uploaded declaration pages into structured information for personal and commercial quoting.


Applications and market submissions[Broker Buddha](https://www.brokerbuddha.com/) Supports insured data capture, ACORD and supplemental applications, document collection, reminders, and multi-carrier submissions.


Personal lines renewal automation[Quandri](https://www.quandri.io/) Reviews renewal policy data, surfaces changes and gaps, requotes selected policies, and prepares personalized client outreach.


**These tools complement an AMS or CRM.** Your system of record still owns the customer and policy record. The AI layer should capture, prepare, or route work, then return usable information to that system with a review trail.


## Best AI for insurance sales: CopyCat


Insurance sales does not end when the carrier returns a price. A producer still has to compare the options, explain the coverage, make a recommendation, and package the result in a document the client can understand.[CopyCat is built for that client-deliverable stage](https://www.runcopycat.com/insurance-proposal-software) .


Producers upload the carrier quotes, binders, policy documents, and supporting files they already receive. CopyCat extracts the relevant values, organizes the comparison, applies the agency's template, and leaves the proposal editable before export. Material figures can link back to the source page, so review does not depend on trusting an unexplained AI answer.


### Commercial lines sales


[For commercial lines](https://www.runcopycat.com/commercial-insurance-proposal-software) , CopyCat handles multi-line accounts and multiple carrier options without flattening the decision to premium alone. Producers can show limits, deductibles, sublimits, exclusions, conditions, subjectivities, fees, financing details, and the recommendation in the agency's own structure. Renewal teams can also compare proposed terms with the expiring program and document the material changes.


### Personal lines sales


[For personal lines](https://www.runcopycat.com/personal-lines-proposal-software) , CopyCat turns home, auto, renters, umbrella, and package quotes into a consistent household proposal. That makes bundled options easier to scan and gives the client one branded summary instead of a thread of carrier PDFs. The producer remains responsible for checking the recommendation and explaining coverage tradeoffs.


### Where CopyCat fits


CopyCat is not a comparative rater and does not return a bindable carrier price. It starts after the quote documents arrive. That is an important distinction: use a rater to obtain options, an AMS to keep the account record, and CopyCat to build the cited sales document the client will actually review.


## Best AI notetakers for broker meetings: Fathom or Circleback


A notetaker earns its place when a producer can stay engaged during a discovery call and still leave with accurate next steps, objections, renewal concerns, and a usable recap. Both Fathom and Circleback cover that core job. The better choice depends on what should happen after the transcript is created.


### Choose Fathom for fast capture and sales follow-up


Fathom publishes support for meeting transcripts, instant summaries, action items, searchable conversation context, custom vocabulary, and CRM connections. It can capture with a meeting bot or through bot-free desktop modes, and its mobile app supports in-person meetings. For a producer who wants to stop splitting attention between the client and a notebook, it is the simpler starting point.


The broker use case is practical: record a prospect call with consent, pull out the operations, payroll, property, vehicle, and renewal-date details, then draft the follow-up while the conversation is fresh. Review the recap before placing anything in the AMS or treating it as a complete fact-find.


### Choose Circleback for customizable post-meeting workflows


Circleback is especially useful when the agency wants the meeting to trigger a repeatable process. Its automations can generate structured AI insights and send notes or updates to systems including Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho, Slack, Notion, monday.com, and Zapier. An agency could, for example, extract renewal timing, named competitors, promised documents, and follow-up owners into consistent fields after every producer meeting.


That flexibility also creates setup work. Define the fields the team actually uses, decide which meetings should trigger each automation, and test the output before allowing it to update a system of record.


## What is the best phone AI for insurance agencies?


Sonant is the strongest fit in this shortlist for phone AI because its product is designed around P&C agencies, brokers, and insurance distributors. It publishes workflows for 24/7 inbound answering, call transfer, quote intake, routine service requests, appointment scheduling, multilingual calls, post-call summaries, and agency-system updates.


That makes it useful at the front of the agency, where a missed new-business call is lost revenue and a routine request can interrupt a producer's sales block. The AI can collect the reason for the call, gather initial details, route the caller, or schedule the next step. Complex coverage questions and distressed clients still need a clean path to a licensed human.


## Best insurance data-intake tool: Canopy Connect


Canopy Connect sits at the beginning of the quoting process. A prospect can give the agency permission to retrieve policy data from the carrier, or upload declaration pages for document extraction. The platform returns structured details such as premiums, coverages, limits, deductibles, drivers, vehicles, properties, and available policy documents across personal and commercial lines.


This is most useful when producers or CSRs spend the first part of every opportunity chasing dec pages and retyping current-policy data. It is not a replacement for discovery: the broker still needs to ask what changed, identify uninsured exposures, and confirm that the retrieved information is current and complete.


## Best AI for applications and submissions: Broker Buddha


Broker Buddha covers the workflow between initial intake and the market. Its current platform includes insured data capture, ACORD and supplemental applications, document collection, e-signature, automated loss-run requests, and a multi-carrier submission workflow with status tracking and quote comparison.


It is a good fit when commercial teams repeatedly request the same information, rebuild last year's application, or manage market status in email and spreadsheets. The clean division of labor is: Broker Buddha helps assemble and move the submission; CopyCat takes the returned quote documents and creates the client-facing sales proposal.


## Best AI for personal lines renewals: Quandri


Quandri focuses on a high-volume job that general AI tools rarely handle end to end: personal lines renewals. It reviews policy data, surfaces coverage changes or gaps, can requote selected at-risk policies, and prepares personalized renewal emails for the client.


That makes it relevant to agencies whose account managers cannot proactively review every home and auto renewal. Set explicit rules for which accounts are requoted, which findings require licensed review, and when the client should receive a human call instead of an automated message.


## How to choose an insurance AI stack


1. **Measure one bottleneck.** Count the weekly hours spent building proposals, writing meeting recaps, or handling routine calls.
2. **Run a real-work test.** Use an actual quote packet, prospect meeting, or call-routing scenario—with appropriate permission and without exposing data outside approved systems.
3. **Inspect the handoff.** Confirm where summaries, tasks, documents, and call notes go, who reviews them, and whether the AMS or CRM remains current.
4. **Review security and control.** Ask about retention, model training, access permissions, audit history, deletion, recording consent, and the process for escalating to a person.
5. **Compare the result, not the demo.** Measure turnaround time, corrections, producer adoption, missed follow-ups, and client experience before expanding the rollout.


## A practical stack for a growing agency


A focused agency stack can stay simple. Canopy Connect collects current-policy data; Broker Buddha organizes a commercial submission; Sonant receives and routes inbound calls; Fathom or Circleback documents producer meetings; Quandri monitors personal lines renewals; and CopyCat turns returned carrier quotes into the proposal used to close the account. Most agencies should adopt only the pieces that solve a measured bottleneck. The AMS or CRM remains the system of record underneath the stack.


The goal is not to automate the relationship. It is to remove the transcription, formatting, and routing work around the relationship, giving producers more time to advise clients and sell.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is the best AI tool for insurance sales?


CopyCat is our recommendation when the sales bottleneck is turning commercial or personal lines quotes into a clear, branded proposal. It is purpose-built for insurance documents, remains editable, and gives reviewers a source trail.


### Should an agency use Fathom or Circleback?


Start with Fathom when easy capture, summaries, action items, and CRM sync are the priority. Evaluate Circleback when the team wants custom fields and more configurable automations after every meeting.


### Can phone AI replace a licensed insurance professional?


It should not be the final authority for advice or complex coverage decisions. Use phone AI for intake, routing, scheduling, routine service collection, and documentation, with clear escalation rules for licensed or judgment-heavy conversations.


### Which tools help with intake, submissions, and renewals?


Use Canopy Connect to collect current policy data, Broker Buddha to organize applications and market submissions, and Quandri to automate personal lines renewal review and outreach. They address different stages, so choose the one closest to the agency's current bottleneck.
